# yantrad

> The Yantra control-plane daemon. Every client talks to this and nothing else; no client ever talks
> directly to a managed machine. An axum server with a read-only JSON API over a background
> snapshot, the writes (`POST /heartbeat`, `new`, and `edit`/`up`/`down`/`resume` per workspace), a
> WebSocket that bridges a workspace's session to a browser, and the dashboard itself. It is an HTTP surface over
> `yantra-core`, not a second copy of the logic.

## Source

- [src/main.rs](src/main.rs): resolves its bind addresses from Tailscale, fails closed, serves `/healthz`, shuts down on SIGTERM. Plain HTTP on 7717; TLS is `tailscale serve`'s (`just https`, port 8443) and never this crate's. The set it binds is also what `write.rs`'s authoriser trusts a forwarded address from (ADR-0017), so it is passed to the router rather than re-derived. The tree itself is composed in `app`, apart from `serve`, so a test can drive it without binding a port (Y-169).
- [src/refresh.rs](src/refresh.rs): one background task per data class, writing `yantra_core::snapshot::Snapshot`. The interval is a constant, low enough to keep the ssh masters warm. No request path touches ssh. The agents task also feeds the notifier, once its reading is already in the model. **Readiness is a class on this sweep rather than a handler that runs `doctor`** (Y-168): it is the dearest look of the five, and a browser polling it per request is the ssh storm this module exists to prevent. It runs at the same interval as the rest because Q6 left nothing to tune and because the agents sweep already runs `claude` on every machine that often — **not** because a slower loop would pay a handshake, which it would not: the other four sweeps hold the `ControlPersist=300` masters open regardless. It takes `write::term()`, since nobody is sitting at this terminal either (I-36). **The attention class is the one that leaves the tailnet, and the only one on an interval of its own** (Y-172): `gh` is a network call, so the rule keeping ssh off the request path binds it for the same reason, but here a faster poll is pure cost — it warms no master and spends the owner's own GitHub quota, which their `gh` and `git push` draw on too. Five minutes, against a measured `X-Poll-Interval: 60` from `/notifications`, which `EVERY` would have polled at twice the rate GitHub asks for. The `Forge` is passed in like the `Inventory`, so the loop is drivable from a fake.
- [src/notify.rs](src/notify.rs): when the diff runs (Y-146). A difference between two consecutive agent readings and nothing more — no poll, no ssh, no timer of its own; [`yantra_core::notify`](../yantra-core/src/notify.rs) decides what a difference *means*. **The first look after a start says nothing** and **a failed send drops that notification** — no queue, no retry, no replay, with `yantra-agent`'s `Log` as the precedent for saying the first failure and swallowing the rest. A look that failed notifies nobody, because an unknown fleet is not a changed one. The pass has a budget well under the refresh interval, so a relay that accepts and never answers cannot push the next look out. **The relay comes from `YANTRA_NTFY_URL` and `YANTRA_NTFY_TOKEN`** (Y-147), read once in `main.rs`: an absent URL is a daemon with no relay and not a refusal to start, the token is read from the environment and nowhere else, and the startup line says which of the two it got because a unit's environment is not the shell's. **The relay is now settable** ([ADR-0021](../../docs/adr/0021-the-relay-is-written-to-an-environment-file.md), Y-199): `/settings` and `yantra relay` write the file the unit reads, so the read path here is unchanged and a new relay reaches this daemon at its next start. **And nothing is pushed while a tab is open** (D3 §13): `Viewers` is one timestamp in memory beside the snapshot, the beacon writes it, and a look taken while somebody is watching still runs its diff and drops what it produced — so closing the tab delivers no backlog. A restart forgets it, which is correct.
- [src/api.rs](src/api.rs): `GET /api/{machines,workspaces,sessions}`, read-only. Every answer says whether the look succeeded, failed or has not happened, and how old it is. **A `workspaces` entry says whether the file loaded** (Y-141) — one that did not is in the list under its name with its reason, rather than turning the whole class into `looked: "failed"`. `machines` also carries each machine's latest heartbeat and its age, joined on the node id; `null` there is *never heard from* and is not a beat that reports zero. DTOs live here rather than as `Serialize` on core's types (ADR-0005) — **`doctor`'s own types are the exception**, because its check names and three states are the JSON contract [D2 §3.1](../../docs/design/02-setup.md) already publishes. **`GET /api/readiness` and `GET /api/machines/{name}/readiness`** (Y-168) serve that sweep, and answer the one check the library cannot: `heartbeat` is *present* with its age where a beat has arrived, *absent* where none has since this daemon started, and *unknown* where the tailnet list holds no node of that name — the beats are keyed on the node id (I-5) and a report names a machine the way a workspace does (ADR-0009). The one-machine route is a **404** for a machine the sweep did not cover, which is the machines no workspace names. **A path under `/api` that no route claims is a JSON 404 here** (Y-169): the nest carries a fallback of its own, because without one the miss reaches the dashboard's SPA fallback and answers `200 text/html` (I-64). **`GET /api/attention`** (Y-173) serves the `gh` reading in the same envelope and blocks on nothing: reviews and issues as two lists under their own names, unread as a count, and an absent or logged-out `gh` as `looked: "failed"` carrying `gh auth login` — never an empty inbox, which is R-23's unplugged sensor reading zero. It is in [contract.gen.ts](../../web/src/contract.gen.ts) since Y-322, which Y-173 deferred until a file in `web/src` read the route — the entry and the type that checks it belong in one change, and splitting them cost two rows.
- [src/refresh.rs](src/refresh.rs): one background task per data class, writing `yantra_core::snapshot::Snapshot`. The interval is a constant, low enough to keep the ssh masters warm. No request path touches ssh. The agents task also feeds the notifier, once its reading is already in the model. **Readiness is a class on this sweep rather than a handler that runs `doctor`** (Y-168): it is the dearest look of the five, and a browser polling it per request is the ssh storm this module exists to prevent. It runs at the same interval as the rest because Q6 left nothing to tune and because the agents sweep already runs `claude` on every machine that often — **not** because a slower loop would pay a handshake, which it would not: the other four sweeps hold the `ControlPersist=300` masters open regardless. It takes `write::term()`, since nobody is sitting at this terminal either (I-36). **The GitHub credential is a sixth task beside it** (Y-175): `gh` runs on this host rather than on a machine in the fleet, and a local probe must not queue behind a `ConnectTimeout` per asleep machine.
- [src/notify.rs](src/notify.rs): when the diff runs (Y-146). A difference between two consecutive agent readings and nothing more — no poll, no ssh, no timer of its own; [`yantra_core::notify`](../yantra-core/src/notify.rs) decides what a difference *means*. **The first look after a start says nothing** and **a failed send drops that notification** — no queue, no retry, no replay, with `yantra-agent`'s `Log` as the precedent for saying the first failure and swallowing the rest. A look that failed notifies nobody, because an unknown fleet is not a changed one. The pass has a budget well under the refresh interval, so a relay that accepts and never answers cannot push the next look out. **The relay comes from `YANTRA_NTFY_URL` and `YANTRA_NTFY_TOKEN`** (Y-147), read once in `main.rs`: an absent URL is a daemon with no relay and not a refusal to start, the token is read from the environment and nowhere else, and the startup line says which of the two it got because a unit's environment is not the shell's. **The relay is now settable** ([ADR-0021](../../docs/adr/0021-the-relay-is-written-to-an-environment-file.md), Y-199): `/settings` and `yantra relay` write the file the unit reads, so the read path here is unchanged and a new relay reaches this daemon at its next start. **And nothing is pushed while a tab is open** (D3 §13): `Viewers` is one timestamp in memory beside the snapshot, the beacon writes it, and a look taken while somebody is watching still runs its diff and drops what it produced — so closing the tab delivers no backlog. A restart forgets it, which is correct.
- [src/api.rs](src/api.rs): `GET /api/{machines,workspaces,sessions}`, read-only. Every answer says whether the look succeeded, failed or has not happened, and how old it is. **A `workspaces` entry says whether the file loaded** (Y-141) — one that did not is in the list under its name with its reason, rather than turning the whole class into `looked: "failed"`. `machines` also carries each machine's latest heartbeat and its age, joined on the node id; `null` there is *never heard from* and is not a beat that reports zero. DTOs live here rather than as `Serialize` on core's types (ADR-0005) — **`doctor`'s own types are the exception**, because its check names and three states are the JSON contract [D2 §3.1](../../docs/design/02-setup.md) already publishes. **`GET /api/readiness` and `GET /api/machines/{name}/readiness`** (Y-168) serve that sweep, and answer the one check the library cannot: `heartbeat` is *present* with its age where a beat has arrived, *absent* where none has since this daemon started, and *unknown* where the tailnet list holds no node of that name — the beats are keyed on the node id (I-5) and a report names a machine the way a workspace does (ADR-0009). The one-machine route is a **404** for a machine the sweep did not cover, which is the machines no workspace names. **A path under `/api` that no route claims is a JSON 404 here** (Y-169): the nest carries a fallback of its own, because without one the miss reaches the dashboard's SPA fallback and answers `200 text/html` (I-64). **`GET /api/readiness/github`** (Y-175) is the readiness answer about *this* host — whether `gh` is installed and logged in where the daemon runs, which is the credential the work inbox reads. A route rather than a tenth check on every report, because an answer about this machine drawn on every machine's card claims something no ssh session asked; and it has no `failed`, since the check carries a look it could not take as *unknown*.
- [src/web.rs](src/web.rs): serves the built dashboard from `YANTRA_WEB`, with a fallback to `index.html` so deep links reach the app. Refuses at startup if that directory holds no `index.html`, and answers a 404 that says how to set it when nothing is configured. **A directory that vanishes after that check answers `503` and logs it**: the startup refusal looks once, and a `YANTRA_WEB` pointing into a deleted git worktree left `ServeDir` answering an empty 404 — the deep link's own status — with nothing in the journal. The check is on the 404 path, which the SPA fallback makes rare while the directory is there; the line is said once and again when it comes back (`yantra-agent`'s `Log`), and the daemon does not exit, because the API, the heartbeat and the terminal socket are all still serving. **The default build embeds nothing** (R-24): a build that wants `web/dist` unconditionally puts npm on every `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` and musl job.
- [src/web/embedded.rs](src/web/embedded.rs): the same dashboard compiled into the binary, so M7's appliance is one file to copy (Y-140). Behind the `embed-dashboard` feature, which is **absent from `default`** — the module is `#[cfg]`'d and `include_dir` is optional, so a default build neither reads `web/dist` nor compiles the macro that would. A `web/dist` with no `index.html` is a *build* error here, which is the directory half's startup refusal moved as early as it can go. **`YANTRA_WEB` wins over it and a set-but-wrong one still refuses**: the embedded copy is fixed at build time and cannot be mistyped, the variable is typed by a person, so the fallible half keeps the refusal rather than being papered over (R-23). Nothing in `just check` or `just ci` may turn the feature on and `--all-features` may appear nowhere; `just no-node` is that omission made into a red build, and [`.github/workflows/embed.yml`](../../.github/workflows/embed.yml) is the one job that builds with it, kept out of `ci.yml` because `ci.yml` has no path filter.
- [src/write.rs](src/write.rs): `POST /api/workspaces`, `PATCH /api/workspaces/{name}` and `POST /api/workspaces/{name}/{up,down,resume}` — the CLI's own verbs and nothing more (`yantra new`, `edit`, `up`, `down`, `resume`). **`POST /api/relay` is `yantra relay`** ([ADR-0021](../../docs/adr/0021-the-relay-is-written-to-an-environment-file.md), Y-199): it writes `/etc/yantra/daemon.env`, then sends a test message to what it wrote, so a **502** means the relay is on disk and the message did not arrive. Nothing reads it back — no route serves the URL or the token. **`POST /api/viewing` is the dashboard saying it is open** (D3 §13), authorised like every other write because it stops this daemon pushing to somebody's phone. Authorised per ADR-0016: the caller's source address is resolved **live** via `whois`, and a node that is not this owner's, or carries tags, is refused 403. A `tailscale` that cannot answer is **503**, never 403 — nothing was decided about the caller. **Which address is resolved depends on the hop** ([ADR-0017](../../docs/adr/0017-the-forwarded-address-is-the-caller-when-the-hop-is-ours.md), Y-118): the TCP peer, unless the peer is one of this daemon's own bind addresses — the shape of a request proxied by `tailscale serve` on this machine — in which case it is `X-Forwarded-For`, which must carry exactly one address or the request is **503**. An absent header is not a refusal; a header sent straight to 7717 is ignored. The verbs that reach a machine await ssh, which the read path may not; `new` touches no machine and answers **409** for a name already taken, returning the created workspace in the body because the read model will not hold it for up to 30 s. `edit` (Y-126) rewrites only the fields the body names — `"startup": null` clears the command, an absent key leaves it, and a body naming nothing is a **400** — and answers the workspace as it now reads, in the same shape `new` answers. It reaches the machine **only** when `machine` really changes, and then refuses rather than strands: a tmux session still open on the machine being left is a **409** (I-30, and `yantra down` clears it), and a machine that could not be asked is a **503** rather than a move (R-23). The refusal is [`edit.rs`](../yantra-core/src/edit.rs)'s; this route only carries it. **`up`, `down` and `resume` map every variant they can refuse with, exhaustively and with no wildcard** (Y-135): **409** where the world already answers and a person changes that answer — an agent holding at claude's trust dialog (I-49), one whose credential the gate did not find (I-44), a session opened as a shell, a workspace that runs something of its own, a `repo` the machine does not have, and a macOS machine with no tmux server, which Yantra will not start there ([ADR-0018](../../docs/adr/0018-the-tmux-server-carries-the-macos-login-session.md) §1, Y-151); **503** where nothing was decided — ssh, tmux, terminfo, a status that could not be read, a `resume` whose two sources disagree (R-23); **500** only for this daemon's own — no state directory, a session id it could not generate. Before this everything but a workspace error fell through to 500, and the dashboard drew a state the daemon had named correctly as *the verb ran and failed*. **`GET` and `POST /api/workspaces/{name}/repair` are the one write this daemon does not compose** ([ADR-0020](../../docs/adr/0020-a-raw-write-only-from-broken-to-valid.md), Y-190): `yantra repair` on the wire, feeding `/w/{name}/repair`. Two refusals bound it — **409** for a file that already loads, since a workspace that works is changed field by field, and **400** for bytes that still will not, carrying the next error rather than a summary, because the caller is answering the one it was shown. `from_repair` is a mapper of its own for that second reason: in `from_workspace` a `Malformed` or a `Blank` is this daemon reading its own files and so a 500, and here it is the bytes the caller sent. **The `GET` lives here rather than in `api.rs`** and is on the same authoriser: a file's raw bytes are the one thing `GET /api/workspaces` does not publish, and it answers the same 409, so opening it is itself the question *is this broken*.
- [src/terminal.rs](src/terminal.rs): `GET /api/workspaces/{name}/terminal`, a WebSocket over [`yantra_core::pty`](../yantra-core/src/pty.rs). An upgrade is a `GET`, so it does **not** inherit `write.rs`'s check and calls `allowed()` by name — `up` starts a process Yantra chose, a terminal runs whatever is typed. Frames carry no envelope: binary is terminal bytes both ways, text is control — `{"rows":…,"cols":…,"term":…}` from the browser, required first because a pty opens with a window and a terminal (the `term` is the dashboard's own constant, never a user's — I-36), and a failure reason from the daemon, which a close frame cannot hold. **The stream is never logged** (Q5), and **never buffered**: a browser that lost its socket opens another, and the tmux on the far side draws the pane for whichever client attaches (Y-132). It holds ssh for as long as someone is looking, which the request path may not — and it does so after the upgrade has answered. **The daemon originates a ping every 20 s and ends the socket after two consecutive misses** (Y-134), which drops the `Terminal` and with it the `ssh`, the pty and the tmux client on the far side. A traffic timer would be wrong in both directions — output in progress is not idleness, silence is not death — and the pong is a protocol frame rather than the stream, so Q5 is untouched: a peer that answers is never closed however long it prints nothing.
- [src/contract.rs](src/contract.rs): tests only. Renders every read route and every write DTO into [`web/src/contract.gen.ts`](../../web/src/contract.gen.ts), TypeScript that `satisfies` the dashboard's own types, and fails when the committed file no longer matches — `just fixtures` rewrites it. The seam between the daemon and the browser, checked rather than kept in step by convention (Y-124).
- [yantrad.service](yantrad.service): the systemd unit for the appliance (Y-142). `Restart=on-failure` with a `RestartSec` chosen against systemd's five-starts-in-ten-seconds limit, because `listen_on`'s refusal is the retry condition and a fast-exiting unit would otherwise sit in `failed` on a box with nobody at it; `After=tailscaled.service`, which orders the start and waits for no address. A **system** unit: a `--user` one cannot order against `tailscaled.service`, which the user manager does not have. [tests/service_unit.rs](tests/service_unit.rs) runs it under a real systemd in a disposable podman container, and `just appliance-install <host>` copies it onto a box beside the binary (Y-145) while [install.sh](../../install.sh) fetches it from the commit the binary was built at (Y-157, [docs/appliance.md](../../docs/appliance.md)).
- [tests/installer.rs](tests/installer.rs): [install.sh](../../install.sh) run **twice** under the same real systemd, as an unprivileged account through `sudo` (Y-158). The second run is the row: an edited `/etc/yantra/agent.env` survives untouched (ADR-0013 §4) and all three binaries are replaced while one of them is executing — with `cp` measured refusing the same write, so the rename is evidence rather than ceremony (Y-145). github.com is [tests/fixture/release.sh](tests/fixture/release.sh) inside the container, which is what lets a **corrupted** archive be served and refused; the cost is that the archive is the fixture's, so its shape is asserted against [release.yml](../../.github/workflows/release.yml). No container holds a `tailscaled`, so the Tailscale step is proved by its report changing when a `tailscale` appears.
- [src/heartbeat.rs](src/heartbeat.rs): `POST /heartbeat`, the write `yantra-agent` makes. 204 with an empty body, a 4 KB limit, strict parsing, and identity taken from the source address rather than the payload. Holds `Beats`, one in-memory row per machine keyed on the node id, overwritten every beat.

## What decides its shape

- [ADR-0005](../../docs/adr/0005-core-logic-in-a-library-crate.md): the logic lives in the library; this crate stays thin.
- [ADR-0013](../../docs/adr/0013-the-heartbeat-carries-only-what-placement-scores.md): what `POST /heartbeat` accepts, why it answers nothing, and why the source address is the identity.
- [ADR-0004](../../docs/adr/0004-rust-for-the-daemon.md): Rust, with axum and tokio. TypeScript belongs to the browser — do not introduce a second runtime here.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): what is already settled, and what to read before starting — including why there is no `--bind` flag.

## Optional

- [tracker.md](tracker.md): the invariants waiting here for the daemon that does not exist yet — SQLite, scheduling, PTY, none of them exercised by shipped code — plus the ones read off the daemon that does: I-58, `listen_on` runs once, so an address that moves under a healthy process is never noticed and `Restart=on-failure` never fires; I-59, the same supervisor re-arming *the first look says nothing* and swallowing every change a restart straddles; I-60, a startup check over something the filesystem owns being no guarantee at request time, enforced in [src/web.rs](src/web.rs); I-63, a machine name reaching `ssh`'s argv from a URL with nothing between it and the process, which ADR-0009 makes unavoidable and nobody had written down; and I-64, a nested router with no fallback of its own handing a miss to the outer one — the dashboard — so an absent `/api` route answered `200 text/html`, enforced in [src/api.rs](src/api.rs). **I-60 and I-64 are the two that shipped code enforces rather than merely records, and the two anyone has seen.**
- [../../tracker.md](../../tracker.md): M4 is the milestone that needs this. Open decisions that affect it are listed there.
- [docs/vision.md](../../docs/vision.md): what the daemon is ultimately for.
